newsitem.title: USA: North Sea Brent paper crude sells cheaper in U.S..
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent paper crude sells cheaper in U.S..

text.p: North Sea Brent paper crude cargoes sold cheaper in the U.S. aftermarket window late Monday, invigorating a quiet foreign crude session, traders said.
"This was a very dead day overall, but the aftermarket was fairly active," said a trader.
May Brent sold for slightly more than one full cargo in an assortment of partial trades. Most of the deals involved a U.K. major and a Wall Street broker.
A total of 600 lots switched hands between $19.45 and $19.37 a barrel, down from the May IPE settlement at $19.52.
A trio of spreads were also confirmed at slightly weaker levels than seen in London.
April/May inter-month Brent was moved at 15 cents twice, bought both times by U.S. refiners, while a third spread was sold at 14 cts, traders said.
